annotations.title: Ordaine Priests.
annotations.text: [1] Though Priests or Bishops may be nominated and elected by the Princes, people, or Patrons of places, according to the vse of the time and diuersitie of Countries and fashions, yet they can not be ordered and consecrated but by a Bishop who was him self rightly ordered or consecrated before, as this Titus was by S. Paul. And here it seemeth that he did not onely consecrate them whom the people had elected before, but him self also made choise of the persons, no mention being here made of any other election popular. [2] Which though it were long vsed in the primitiue Church, yet for diuers causes and specially for continual tumultes, partialities, and disorders which S. Augustine much complaineth of in his time, was iustly taken away, and other better meanes of their designement appointed. See Conc. Laodic. cap. 12. 13. S. August. de adult. coniug. li. 2. c. 20. Ep. 110. and Possid. in vita Aug. c. 8. [3] And that the ordering of Priests or imposition of hands to that purpose, belongeth onely to Bishops, and to no inferior Priests or other persons, it is plaine by the Apostolike practise set downe in the Scriptures, namely in the Actes, and in the Epistles to Timothee and Titus. And S. Hierom, who seemeth sometimes to say that in the primitiue Church there was no great difference betwixt a Bishop and Priest, yet he euer excepteth giuing holy Orders, which preeminence he attributeth to Bishops onely. ep. 85. as he doth also Confirming the Baptized by giuing them the holy Ghost through imposition of hand and holy Chrisme. Dial. cont. Lucifer. c. 4. [4] Note also that Aërius was of old condemned of heresie, for holding that there was no difference betwixt a Priest and a Bishop. Epiph. hær. 75. August. hær. 53. [5] Note lastly the fraudulent translation of the Heretikes alwaies, turning for Priests (which here is euident to be a calling of Order and office) elders, saying, That thou ordaine Elders. which in our vulgar tonge signifieth the age, and not the Office properly: and al this for hatred of Priests.

notes.text: Priests must be consecrated by Bishops only.
The popular election of the Cleargie taken away.
The preeminence of a Bishop aboue a Priest.
To put no difference betwene them is Aërius heresie.

annotations.title: Of one wife.
annotations.text: ◦ To that which is said vpon the like wordes 1 Tim. 3: adde this testimonie of S. Epiphanius li. 3. to. 2. cont. hæres. in fine. Holy Priesthod, saith he, for the most part procedeth of Virgins: and if not of virgins, yet of them that liue a sole or single life: but and if the single and sole persons suffice not to the Ministerie, of such as conteine from their wiues, or after once marying remaine widowes. For, him that hath been maried twise, it is not lawful to take to Priesthod &c. If you list to see the causes why bigamie is forbidden them that are to be Priests, and continencie required of the Clergie, see the same author li. 2. to. 1. hæres. 59. S. Ambrose li. 1. Offic. c. 50. and vpon 1 Tim. 3. S. Augustine de bono Coniugal. c. 18. S. Hierom ep. 50 c. 5 ad Pammachium, and against Iouinian li. 1 c. 19. S. Leo ep. 87. and other auncient authors. [1] And if the studious reader peruse al antiquitie, he shal finde al notable Bishops and Priests of Gods Church to haue been single, or continent from their wiues, if any were maried before they came to the Clergie. So was S. Paul, and exhorteth al men to the like: 1 Cor. 7, 7. So were al the Apostles after they folowed Christ, as S. Hierom witnesseth, affirming that our Lord loued Iohn specially for his virginitie. Apol. ad Pammach. c. 8. & li. 1 cont. Iouin. c. 14. S. Ignatius ep. 6 ad Philadelph. saith of the said Iohn, and of Timothee, Titus, Euodius, Clement, that they liued and died in chastitie, reckening vp of the old Testament diuers notable personages that did the same, as Elias, Iesus Naue (otherwise called Iosue) Melchisedec, Elisæus, Hieremie, Iohn Baptist. No man is ignorant that al the notable fathers of the Greeke and Latin Church liued chast: Athanasius; Basil, Nazianzene, Chrysostom, Cyprian, Hilarie (who entered into holy Orders after his wiues death) Ambrose, Hierom, Augustine, Leo, Gregorie the great. Certaine other notable fathers had once wiues, but no holy men euer vsed them, much lesse maried, after they were in holy Orders. [2] A maruelous thing, that so many heretofore should haue the gift of chastitie then, and now so few, if the Protestants say true, that skarse one among them in our age of al their sectes, euen of their principal Superintendents, hath had it.

notes.text: The notable men of both Testaments, that liued continently from wiues.
Only the Protestants complaine that they haue not the gift of chastitie.
